purpose: Distinguish wrong-reward-induced target transfer from general gold-training and base-selection effects after the heterogeneous R10 development screen.

observed_problem: two task-pair means were positive but two of eight stack effects were negative
one of five identity effects was negative
only two of eight stacks placed the identity alignment in the top five percent of 120 deterministic bijections
the global identity-matched absolute effect was negative even though diagonal excess was positive

bug_update.reward: gold candidate plus the frozen wrong candidate for source identity r

aggregation: equal target off-diagonal identity within source identity
equal mapping and direction within task pair

required_secondary_readouts: gold-only update norm as diagnostic only
all 120 deterministic identity alignment ranks with no inferential p-value

execution_cost_if_approved.estimated_fraction_of_r10_update_work: approximately one fifth before process startup and base-scoring overhead
execution_cost_if_approved.cost_note: Reviewer must decide whether cross-release reuse is acceptable or both arms must be rerun in a new counterbalanced release.

decision_boundary.this_bridge_can_establish: whether R10 diagonal excess survives subtraction of general gold-only learning on the same frozen development assets

open_review_questions: Is gold-only subtraction sufficient under one-step unclipped manual SGD, or is an explicit wrong-only arm required?
Can immutable R10 bug arms be reused, or must bug and gold-only arms be rerun in one new counterbalanced release?
Does frozen pre state suffice as no-op, or is a separately executed no-op process required?
Must a non-affine codebook without the shared affine anchor be added before any new model action?
What practical margin can be justified independently of R10 outcomes?
